newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey will lift emergency rule soon - Erbakan.
newsitem.headline: Turkey will lift emergency rule soon - Erbakan.

text.p: Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan vowed on Tuesday to abolish emergency rule imposed in Turkey's mainly-Kurdish provinces to counter an armed Kurdish insurgency.
"Emergency rule will be abolished in the near term," Erbakan told a meeting of his Islamist Welfare Party deputies. He gave no precise time scale.
Emergency rule has been in force in 10 Turkish provinces since 1987 as part of Ankara's strategy to combat Kurdish rebels fighting for self-rule in southeastern Turkey.
More tham 21,000 people have died in the 12-year conflict between Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas and Turkish armed forces.

Erbakan told deputies there had been a marked decline in rebel activities in Mardin and Elazig provinces. Emergency rule is to be abolished in Mardin, and Elazig will be taken off the list of provinces neighbouring the emergency rule region where the military also has extensive powers, he said.
Turkey's powerful National Security Council recommended last Thursday that emergency rule be lifted in Mardin.

Erbakan has said he will end the fighting in the spirit of "Moslem brotherhood", but a tentative peace bid by one of his MPs has faded away under pressure from the military and hardliners in parliament.
Like his predecessors, Erbakan has refused to negotiate with the rebels.
